scales.name: Earthquake magnitude
scales.question: Moment magnitude. Each whole step releases about 32 times more energy.

items.name: L'Aquila, 2009
items.fact: Six Italian scientists were convicted (later acquitted) over their risk statements before this quake.

items.name: Sichuan, 2008
items.fact: The Sichuan quake was felt as far away as Beijing and Bangkok.

items.name: Indian Ocean, 2004
items.fact: Its tsunami reached the coast of Africa, about 5,000 km away.

items.name: Valdivia, Chile, 1960
items.fact: Valdivia is the most powerful earthquake ever recorded.

items.name: Kobe, 1995
items.fact: The Kobe earthquake destroyed much of the city's port.

scales.name: What wind force is this?
scales.question: The Beaufort scale describes wind by what you can see it doing, from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane force).

items.name: Leaves and small twigs in constant motion; light flags extended
items.fact: Force 3 is a 'gentle breeze'.

items.name: Sea completely white with driving spray
items.fact: Force 12 is 'hurricane force': 118 km/h or more.

items.name: Smoke rises straight up
items.fact: Admiral Francis Beaufort created the scale in 1805 for sailors.

items.name: Trees uprooted; considerable damage to buildings
items.fact: Force 10, a 'storm', is seldom experienced inland.

items.name: Twigs break off trees
items.fact: Force 8 is a 'gale'.

scales.name: Energy density
scales.question: Calories (kcal) in 100 grams of each.

items.name: Olive oil
items.fact: Oil is pure fat, the most energy-dense nutrient.

items.name: Honey
items.fact: Honey found in ancient Egyptian tombs was still edible.

items.name: Avocado
items.fact: Avocados ripen only after they're picked.

items.name: Butter
items.fact: Butter is about 80% fat.

items.name: Cucumber
items.fact: Cucumbers are about 95% water.

scales.name: Running time
scales.question: How long each film is, in minutes.

items.name: Back to the Future (1985)
items.fact: The time machine needs exactly 88 mph.

items.name: Toy Story (1995)
items.fact: Toy Story was the first entirely computer-animated feature film.

items.name: Lawrence of Arabia (1962)
items.fact: Lawrence of Arabia has no speaking roles for women.

items.name: Titanic (1997)
items.fact: Titanic won 11 Oscars.

items.name: The Dark Knight (2008)
items.fact: Heath Ledger won a posthumous Oscar for playing the Joker.

scales.name: Mohs hardness
scales.question: Which scratches which? 1 is soft as talc, 10 is diamond.

items.name: Glass
items.fact: A steel knife and window glass are close in hardness.

items.name: Diamond
items.fact: One step above corundum, but about four times as hard.

items.name: Calcite
items.fact: Calcite makes up limestone and marble.

items.name: Topaz
items.fact: Pure topaz is colorless; most blue topaz in shops has been treated.

items.name: Potassium metal
items.fact: Potassium is soft enough to cut with a butter knife.

scales.name: River length
scales.question: Length from source to mouth in kilometers. Each gridline step is ten times longer.

items.name: Loire
items.fact: The Loire is France's longest river.

items.name: Nile
items.fact: The Nile and the Amazon still compete for 'longest river', depending on how you measure.

items.name: Jordan
items.fact: The Jordan flows into the Dead Sea, the lowest place on land.

items.name: Hudson
items.fact: The Hudson's lower half is a tidal estuary.

items.name: Colorado
items.fact: The Colorado carved the Grand Canyon.

scales.name: Loudness
scales.question: Sound pressure level in decibels. Every +10 dB sounds roughly twice as loud.

items.name: Krakatoa eruption, 165 km away
items.fact: The 1883 Krakatoa eruption was heard nearly 5,000 km away.

items.name: Quietest room on Earth (Microsoft's anechoic chamber)
items.fact: Decibels can go below zero: zero is only the faintest sound a typical ear can hear.

items.name: Threshold of pain
items.fact: Around 120–134 dB sound starts to physically hurt.

items.name: Vacuum cleaner
items.fact: 85 dB over long periods can damage hearing.

items.name: A very calm room
items.fact: A quiet bedroom at night is around 25 dB.

scales.name: How deep down
scales.question: Meters below the water surface. Each gridline step is ten times deeper.

items.name: Where sunlight fades out
items.fact: Below about 200 m there isn't enough light for photosynthesis.

items.name: Challenger Deep
items.fact: The pressure in Challenger Deep is over 1,000 times that at the surface.

items.name: Crater Lake (deepest point)
items.fact: Crater Lake is the deepest lake in the United States.

items.name: Cuvier's beaked whale dive
items.fact: One Cuvier's beaked whale stayed under for 3 hours 42 minutes.

items.name: Recreational scuba limit
items.fact: Below about 30 m, nitrogen starts to make divers feel drunk.

scales.name: When was it completed?
scales.question: The year each landmark was finished or opened.

items.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
items.fact: Notre-Dame reopened in December 2024 after the 2019 fire.

items.name: Westminster Hall
items.fact: Westminster Hall is the oldest part of the Houses of Parliament.

items.name: Brooklyn Bridge
items.fact: P. T. Barnum walked 21 elephants across the Brooklyn Bridge to prove it was safe.

items.name: Château de Chambord
items.fact: Its double-helix staircase may have been designed by Leonardo da Vinci.

items.name: St Paul's Cathedral
items.fact: St Paul's survived the Blitz almost untouched.

scales.name: How thick and gooey?
scales.question: Viscosity in millipascal-seconds (water is about 1). Each gridline step is ten times thicker.

items.name: Honey
items.fact: Honey's thickness depends strongly on its water content.

items.name: SAE 30 motor oil
items.fact: The number in motor-oil grades is a viscosity class.

items.name: Pitch (tar)
items.fact: In the Pitch Drop Experiment, running since 1927, a drop falls about once a decade.

items.name: Gasoline
items.fact: Gasoline flows more easily than water.

items.name: Blood
items.fact: Blood is 3 to 6 times as viscous as water.

scales.name: Country size
scales.question: Land and water area in square kilometers. Each gridline step is ten times bigger.

items.name: Singapore
items.fact: Singapore is the #178 largest of 197 countries by area.

items.name: Switzerland
items.fact: Switzerland is the #133 largest of 197 countries by area.

items.name: India
items.fact: India is the #8 largest of 197 countries by area.

items.name: Nauru
items.fact: Nauru is the #195 largest of 197 countries by area.

items.name: Vatican City
items.fact: Vatican City is the #197 largest of 197 countries by area.

scales.name: How much does the sting hurt?
scales.question: Schmidt sting pain index: entomologist Justin Schmidt rated the pain of insect stings he received, from 1 (mild) to 4 (excruciating).

items.name: Trap-jaw ant
items.fact: Trap-jaw ants snap their jaws shut faster than almost any other animal movement.

items.name: Red fire ant
items.fact: Schmidt: "Like walking across a shag carpet and reaching for the light switch."

items.name: Honey bee sting on the tongue
items.fact: Schmidt: "For 10 minutes life is not worth living."

items.name: Bullet ant
items.fact: Schmidt: "Like walking over flaming charcoal with a 3-inch nail embedded in your heel."

items.name: Jack jumper ant
items.fact: Schmidt: "The oven mitt had a hole in it when you pulled the cookies out of the oven."

scales.name: How fast?
scales.question: Top or typical speed in km/h. Each gridline step is ten times faster.

items.name: Earth orbiting the Sun
items.fact: You're moving around the Sun at about 30 km every second.

items.name: Light
items.fact: Nothing travels faster than light in a vacuum.

items.name: Skydiver falling face-down
items.fact: Falling head-first instead can be much faster.

items.name: Average walking speed
items.fact: Above about 7 km/h it becomes more efficient to run than to walk.

items.name: World's fastest snail (record)
items.fact: The record snail covered 33 cm in 2 minutes.

scales.name: Density
scales.question: Kilograms per cubic meter (water is 1,000). Each gridline step is ten times denser.

items.name: Air at sea level
items.fact: A cubic meter of air weighs about as much as a bag of sugar.

items.name: Osmium
items.fact: Osmium is the densest naturally occurring element.

items.name: Fresh water
items.fact: Water is densest at about 4 °C.

items.name: Hydrogen gas
items.fact: Hydrogen is the lightest element and the most common in the universe.

items.name: Styrofoam
items.fact: Styrofoam is about 95% air.

scales.name: Caffeine
scales.question: Milligrams of caffeine per serving.

items.name: Decaf coffee (207 ml)
items.fact: Decaf isn't caffeine-free, just much lower.

items.name: Jolt Cola (695 ml)
items.fact: Jolt's 1980s slogan was 'All the sugar and twice the caffeine'.

items.name: Unsweetened cocoa powder (100 g)
items.fact: Cocoa powder is where chocolate's caffeine comes from.

items.name: Excedrin painkiller tablet
items.fact: Caffeine makes some painkillers work better.

items.name: Drip coffee (207 ml)
items.fact: Filter coffee is one of the strongest everyday caffeine sources.

scales.name: Melting point
scales.question: The temperature where each one turns to liquid.

items.name: Tungsten
items.fact: Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metals, which made it ideal for light-bulb filaments.

items.name: Mercury
items.fact: Mercury is the only metal that's liquid at room temperature.

items.name: Zinc
items.fact: Zinc coats steel to stop it rusting (galvanizing).

items.name: Iron
items.fact: Iron is the most common element on Earth by mass.

items.name: Gold
items.fact: All the gold ever mined would fit in a cube about 22 m on each side.

scales.name: Chili heat
scales.question: Scoville heat units: how many times an extract must be diluted before you can't taste the burn.

items.name: Bird's eye chili
items.fact: Bird's eye chilies are a staple of Thai cooking.

items.name: Jalapeño
items.fact: Smoked, dried jalapeños are called chipotles.

items.name: Ghost pepper
items.fact: The ghost pepper was the first pepper measured at over one million SHU.

items.name: Pure capsaicin
items.fact: Pure capsaicin is the benchmark at the top of the scale.

items.name: Banana pepper
items.fact: Banana peppers are so mild that some taste almost sweet.

scales.name: How much data?
scales.question: Size in bytes. Each gridline step is ten times more.

items.name: Five-minute song at CD quality
items.fact: A CD stores sound as 44,100 samples per second, per channel.

items.name: Single-layer DVD
items.fact: A DVD holds about 7 times as much as a CD.

items.name: A 500-page book as plain text
items.fact: Plain text is tiny: a whole novel fits in under a megabyte.

items.name: Human memory (Kurzweil's estimate)
items.fact: Futurist Ray Kurzweil estimated a human's functional memory at about 1.25 TB.

items.name: Facebook's data warehouse (2014)
items.fact: In 2014 Facebook's warehouse was growing by about 0.6 PB a day.

scales.name: Boiling point
scales.question: The temperature where each one boils, at normal air pressure.

items.name: Water
items.fact: On top of Mount Everest water boils at only about 70 °C.

items.name: Gold
items.fact: Gold can be beaten so thin that light shines through it.

items.name: Lead
items.fact: Lead boils at a temperature hotter than lava from many volcanoes.

items.name: Sodium
items.fact: Sodium-vapor street lamps glow orange.

items.name: Tungsten
items.fact: Tungsten boils at about the temperature of the Sun's surface.

scales.name: Capital city population
scales.question: People living in the city itself (not the wider metro area). Each gridline step is ten times more.

items.name: Thimphu (Bhutan)
items.fact: Thimphu is the #168 most populous of 203 national capitals.

items.name: Moscow (Russia)
items.fact: Moscow is the #5 most populous of 203 national capitals.

items.name: Roseau (Dominica)
items.fact: Roseau is the #193 most populous of 203 national capitals.

items.name: Vatican City
items.fact: Vatican City is the #201 most populous of 203 national capitals.

items.name: Paris (France)
items.fact: Paris is the #56 most populous of 203 national capitals.

scales.name: How sweet?
scales.question: Sweetness compared with table sugar (sugar = 1). Each gridline step is ten times sweeter.

items.name: Cyclamate
items.fact: Cyclamate was discovered in 1937 by a student who noticed his cigarette tasted sweet.

items.name: Neotame
items.fact: Neotame is a close relative of aspartame, about 40 times sweeter.

items.name: Saccharin
items.fact: Saccharin, from 1879, is the oldest artificial sweetener.

items.name: Lugduname
items.fact: Lugduname is one of the sweetest substances known; it has never been approved as food.

items.name: Table sugar (sucrose)
items.fact: Sucrose is the yardstick: everything else is measured against it.

scales.name: Voltage
scales.question: How much electrical tension? Each gridline step is ten times more.

items.name: Biggest human-made DC voltage
items.fact: It was produced by a Van de Graaff generator at Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

items.name: Brain waves (EEG) at the scalp
items.fact: Brain waves are measured in millionths of a volt.

items.name: Nerve cell at rest
items.fact: Every nerve cell is a tiny battery, kept charged by pumping ions.

items.name: Electric fence
items.fact: Electric fences use high voltage but very short, low-current pulses.

items.name: Car battery
items.fact: A car battery has six cells of about 2 volts each.

scales.name: Distance from the Sun
scales.question: Average distance from the Sun in astronomical units (1 AU is Earth's distance). Each gridline step is ten times farther.

items.name: Mars
items.fact: Mars is named after the Roman god of war.

items.name: Uranus
items.fact: Uranus was the first planet found with a telescope, in 1781.

items.name: Mercury
items.fact: A year on Mercury lasts 88 Earth days.

items.name: Eris
items.fact: Eris is almost exactly the same size as Pluto.

items.name: Jupiter
items.fact: Jupiter takes almost 12 years to orbit the Sun.

scales.name: How tall
scales.question: Height from base to top, in meters. Each gridline step is ten times taller.

items.name: Angel Falls
items.fact: Angel Falls is the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall.

items.name: Great Pyramid of Giza (original)
items.fact: It was the tallest human-made structure for almost 4,000 years.

items.name: Adult giraffe
items.fact: A giraffe's neck has seven vertebrae, the same as yours.

items.name: Kilimanjaro
items.fact: Kilimanjaro is the tallest free-standing mountain on land.

items.name: Christ the Redeemer statue
items.fact: The statue is struck by lightning several times a year.

scales.name: Lifespan
scales.question: Typical (or record) life length, from hours to millennia.

items.name: Methuselah bristlecone pine
items.fact: Methuselah's exact location is kept secret to protect it.

items.name: Horse
items.fact: A horse's age can be estimated from its teeth.

items.name: Greenland shark (estimate)
items.fact: Greenland sharks grow only about 1 cm a year.

items.name: Adult mayfly
items.fact: Adult mayflies have no working mouths; they live only to mate.

items.name: Fruit fly
items.fact: Fruit flies are one of the most studied animals in genetics.

scales.name: Radiation dose
scales.question: Effective dose in sieverts (Sv). Each gridline step is ten times more.

items.name: Eating a banana
items.fact: Bananas are slightly radioactive because they contain potassium-40.

items.name: Yearly limit for US radiation workers
items.fact: Limits for workers are set well below doses that cause any visible harm.

items.name: Dose fatal to half of people (short exposure)
items.fact: Doses spread out over time are far less harmful than the same dose all at once.

items.name: Dental X-rays
items.fact: A set of dental X-rays is about the same as a day of natural background radiation.

items.name: Mammogram
items.fact: Mammograms use low-energy X-rays.

scales.name: How heavy?
scales.question: Mass, from milligrams to millions of tonnes. Each gridline step is ten times heavier.

items.name: Pando aspen grove
items.fact: Pando is a single aspen clone with about 47,000 stems, maybe the heaviest living organism.

items.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
items.fact: The Great Pyramid is made of about 2.3 million blocks.

items.name: Mosquito
items.fact: Smaller mosquito species weigh about 2.5 milligrams.

items.name: Adult mouse
items.fact: A house mouse weighs 20–40 grams.

items.name: Hubble Space Telescope
items.fact: Hubble weighs about as much as two adult elephants.

scales.name: pH
scales.question: How acidic or basic is it? 7 is neutral; every step down is ten times more acidic.

items.name: Orange juice
items.fact: Orange juice is acidic enough to soften tooth enamel.

items.name: Battery acid
items.fact: Car battery acid is sulfuric acid, strong enough to burn skin.

items.name: Household ammonia
items.fact: Never mix ammonia with bleach: together they release toxic gas.

items.name: Lye (drain cleaner)
items.fact: Lye has been used for centuries to make soap.

items.name: Pure water
items.fact: Pure water is neutral, but rainwater is slightly acidic from dissolved CO₂.

scales.name: Surface gravity
scales.question: How hard you'd be pulled down standing on each world. Each gridline step is ten times stronger.

items.name: Mars
items.fact: On Mars you'd weigh a bit over a third of your Earth weight.

items.name: Ceres
items.fact: Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt.

items.name: Ganymede
items.fact: Ganymede is bigger than the planet Mercury.

items.name: Jupiter
items.fact: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

items.name: Venus
items.fact: Venus is almost Earth's twin in size and gravity.

scales.name: Energy density
scales.question: Calories (kcal) in 100 grams of each.

items.name: Banana
items.fact: Bananas are slightly radioactive because of their potassium.

items.name: Walnuts
items.fact: Walnuts are among the oldest tree foods known.

items.name: Cheddar cheese
items.fact: Cheddar is named after a village in Somerset, England.

items.name: Peanut butter
items.fact: Peanuts are legumes, related to beans and peas.

items.name: Watermelon
items.fact: Watermelon is a berry, botanically speaking.
